newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania 1997 foreign debt limit seen at $3.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Romania 1997 foreign debt limit seen at $3.0 bln.

text.p: Romania's central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said the 1997 external debt limit would be close to this year's $3.0 billion, the independent Mediafax news agency said on Thursday.
Isarescu told Mediafax his bank would draw medium- and long-term loans worth up to $1.5 billion from international markets. The rest will be raised by the Finance Ministry.
Central bank officials were unavailable for comment.

With external debt servicing estimated at some $1.2 billion in 1997, the central bank will have to maintain the foreign exchange reserve levels it managed to build up this year, when it drew $1.4 billion from the international markets.
Latest data showed the central bank's foreign exchange reserves were $1.0 billion in October. The figure does not include some 87 tonnes of gold in reserves.
Virtually absent from world capital markets since the 1980s, Romania resumed activity in 1995 with syndicated loans, followed by its first Samurai and Eurobond issues this year.
It got its first rating from major agencies -- a BB plus from Japan Credit Rating Agency, BB-minus by Standard and Poors and Britain's IBCA and BA-three by Moody's Investors Service.
Romania's medium- and long-term external debt stood at $6.255 billion at end-September, when short-term liabilities were $728.5 million.

Some 43 percent of end-September medium- and long-term debt comes from international institutions, including the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
